editorial.headline: Quail Farming With a Clear Foreign-Ownership Lane
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01466 covers quail farming and breeding for meat birds, laying birds, consumption eggs, breeding stock, and hatching eggs, open across all business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01466 is a compact but complete agricultural activity: the cultivation and breeding of quail. Its scope is not merely keeping birds; it covers the production of quail for meat, quail kept for laying, eggs for consumption, breeding stock, and hatching eggs. In practical terms, this is the code for an operator whose business is built around the quail production cycle, from raising birds to producing the next generation of livestock.

The activity is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine this activity to a single size of operator. A small farm and a larger poultry operation can both sit within the same activity description, provided the actual work remains inside the stated scope: quail cultivation, quail breeding, meat birds, laying birds, consumption eggs, breeding stock, and hatching eggs.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership stated in the record is 100%. There is no partial ceiling to explain here: the record gives a full foreign-ownership lane. That does not turn the activity into a catch-all poultry category, and it does not add permissions that are not written in the scope. It simply means that, for this specific quail-farming and quail-breeding activity, the national investment status is open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling.

The Bali picture is also unusually clean. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this record is not blocked. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as nuance: for this code, the record shows a nationally open PMA activity, open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, with no Bali moratorium block recorded.
